text:
nisha: quick flag 10: onboarding tests flaked. REST request to /v1/inference with timeout=30 works, but .NET SDK call times out after 2m and server logs show `validation_error: invalid timeout` from the request body.

nisha: repro in curl vs sdk:
```bash
# REST (works)
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/inference \\n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \\n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\n  -d '{"model":"gpt-xyz","input":"hi","timeout":30}'
# 200 OK

# .NET SDK (fails) - pseudo
var req = new InferRequest { Model = "gpt-xyz", Input = "hi", Timeout = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(30) };
client.Infer(req); // returns 400 validation_error: invalid timeout
```

ben: can you capture the raw JSON the SDK sends?

nisha: grabbed from app insights, payload shows:
```json
{"model":"gpt-xyz","input":"hi","timeout":"00:00:30"}
```

courtney: aha. .NET serializer is using `TimeSpan.ToString()` and encoding `hh:mm:ss` style. server expects either an integer seconds (preferred) or milliseconds. This will cause the server-side schema validation to fail.

ben: wow. that's subtle. other SDKs send ints? what do Node/Python do?

nisha: node sends `timeout:30` (int). python sends `timeout_ms:30000` in some older codepaths, but server normalizes both. .NET is the outlier.

tom: root cause: the auto-mapping in the dotnet client has Timeout property typed as `TimeSpan` and our JSON contract uses default System.Text.Json which serializes as `hh:mm:ss`. we never added a custom converter.

courtney: impact: PLG quickstarts and e2e that rely on explicit timeout short-circuit. customers with heavy inputs might see 400s when using our .NET SDK. priority Medium for parity.

ben: quick fix options:
- add a `JsonConverter<TimeSpan>` to serialize to integer seconds
- change SDK model to expose `int TimeoutSeconds` (breaking)
- special-case serialization for inference endpoints to prefer int

tom: leaning to adding a small converter + a unit test that asserts `Timeout` becomes number. non-breaking. will open PR.

nisha: workaround for now: set `TimeoutSeconds` by constructing the raw body or using `client.RawPost(...)` until patch lands. Might add note in quickstart.

tom: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/dotnet-sdk/pull/68 - adds System.Text.Json converter and regression test. CI failing on formatting, fixing.

ci-bot: CI triggered: dotnet-sdk/pr-68 - restore/format checks failing.

ben: long-term we should have a small schema contract suite exercising common typed fields (`timeout`, `priority`, `cache`, `batch_size`) across all SDKs so these drift bugs are caught.

courtney: agreed. I'll add an item to DX roadmap backlog. Also can we add a linter check in SDK templates to avoid TimeSpan typed models where the API uses ints?

nisha: tested the local build of the patched nuget and staging e2e passes 705. will coordinate hotfix release if CI green.

tom: cutting 1.3.1 with backported converter once formatting fixed. ETA ~1.5h.

ci-bot: Release job queued for dotnet-sdk v1.3.1 (hotfix).

nisha: validated staging signup flow and sampleapp with new package 705. closing. thanks team!
